cases.description: Publication 517 (2025) lists this among the exceptions to SE tax on ministerial earnings: "You are subject only to the social security laws of a foreign country under the provisions of a social security agreement between the United States and that country." 26 U.S.C. 1401(c): "During any period in which there is in effect an agreement entered into pursuant to section 233 of the Social Security Act with any foreign country, the self-employment income of an individual shall be exempt" to the extent the agreement subjects it "exclusively to the laws applicable to the social security system of such foreign country". Pub. L. 95-216 section 317(b)(1) added the subsection ("Subsec. (c). Pub. L. 95–216, § 317(b)(1) , added subsec. (c)."), and section 317(a) added section 233 itself (42 U.S.C. 433, "as added Pub. L. 95–216, title III, § 317(a) , Dec. 20, 1977"), whose (c)(1)(B)(i) has every agreement place self-employment in one system "but not under both". Neither captured page gives section 317 another date (the 1401 page's Effective Date of 1977 Amendment note, section 104, covers title I only), so the condition carries the limit the subsection states, an agreement under section 233 in effect for the period, and no worker meets it before December 20, 1977. Pub. L. 98-21 section 124(b) redesignated the subsection (d) and Pub. L. 101-508 made it (c) again; Pub. L. 108-203 section 415 replaced "to taxes or contributions for similar purposes under" with "exclusively to the laws applicable to", and a person subject only to the partner country's laws meets both wordings. Review r7 M-2 dates the exemption on these captures; the pre-1983 open cases it closes rested on Pub. L. 98-21 section 322(c), the date of 411(b)'s section 433 exception, not of 1401(c). It overrides cnmi_noncitizen_resident_ministry and ministry_without_exemption_or_vow: on either CNMI reading the exemption leaves the earnings noncovered.

worked_examples.source_passage: Pat Brown and Chris Green are members of a religious order and have taken vows of poverty. They renounce all claims to their earnings. The earnings belong to the order. Pat is a licensed attorney. The superiors of the order instructed Pat to get a job with a law firm. Pat joined a law firm as an employee and, as requested, the firm made the salary payments directly to the order. Chris is a secretary. The superiors of the order instructed Chris to accept a job with the business office of the church that supervises the order. Chris took the job and gave all earnings to the order. Pat's services aren't duties required by the order. Pat’s earnings are subject to social security and Medicare tax under FICA and to federal income tax. Chris' services are duties required by the order. Chris is acting as an agent of the order and not as an employee of a third party. Chris doesn't include the earnings in gross income, and they aren't subject to income tax withholding or to social security and Medicare tax under FICA or SECA.

cases.description: 410(a)(8)(A) excludes order duties by "a member of a religious order" unless an order election is in effect, and 411(c)'s closing sentence keeps 411(c)(4)'s exclusion from self-employment for every member "who has taken a vow of poverty as a member of such order". Neither limits the exclusion to an active member, so a vowed member retired for old age or total disability is excluded too. 410(a)(8)(A) lifts the exclusion only "if an election of coverage under section 3121(r) ... is in effect with respect to such order, or with respect to the autonomous subdivision thereof to which such member belongs", so another subdivision's election leaves it in place (3121(r)(1)(B)).

cases.description: 3121(r)(2) defines a member "For purposes of this subsection" as one who performs tasks usually required "(and to the extent usually required)" of an active member and is not retired for old age or total disability, and 3121(r)(1)(C) deems only such a member's duties to be employment. A vowed member outside that definition gets no deemed wages under the election, and 411(c)'s closing sentence keeps the vow-of-poverty exclusion from self-employment, so the order election does not cover her duties.Noncovered whether or not an election is in effect: with no election 410(a)(8)(A) excludes the duties (vow_duties_without_election), and with one this member is outside what 3121(r) makes employment, so the case reads no election and ranks above election_status_not_established (review r6 M-2).

3121(r)(1)(C) deems the order duties of a member, as 3121(r)(2) defines one (active, and not retired for old age or total disability), to be performed as an employee of the order; use the value of perquisites subject to the statutory floor. A subdivision's election applies only "to all current and future members of such order who belong to such subdivision" (3121(r)(1)(B)).POMS RS 01901.620 B.4 conditions a member's service abroad on the election, citizenship (from 1984, citizenship or residence) and membership: "Services performed by members of religious orders working outside the U.S. are covered if: • the order has elected coverage, • the member is a U.S. citizen, or effective January 1, 1984, a resident alien, and • the individual remains a member of the order even though their services may be directed by a third party outside the U.S., the right to direct and control remains with the member's order within the U.S." Its third bullet makes remaining a member the condition: direction by a third party abroad leaves the right to direct and control with the order, so no case excludes a member abroad on control alone (review r6 M-4; POMS NL 00711.065 1331.3 B lists the same three conditions).

Mandatory coverage, including optionals and ineligibles, unless a statutory exclusion applies. Membership only in a system that fails the IRS qualified-system standards (POMS SL 50001.501 B) does not defeat it (410(a)(7)(F)). 410(a)(7)(F) asks whether the individual is "a member of a retirement system of such State, political subdivision, or instrumentality", and 26 C.F.R. 31.3121(b)(7)-2(c)(2) answers it "on an entity-by-entity rather than a position-by-position basis": a member through one position "is generally treated as a member of a retirement system with respect to all service performed for the same State, political subdivision or instrumentality in any other positions" (Example 1: a county plan member's part-time county service in a position the plan excludes stays excluded), while "A State is a separate entity from its political subdivisions" (Example 2: a State plan member's part-time service for a city whose plan she is not in is not excluded). A statewide system counts when the employing entity takes part in it: (e)(2)(v) speaks of "a retirement system maintained by multiple States, political subdivisions or instrumentalities thereof (including the current employer)", (d)(4)(ii) of "a school district that participates in a state-wide teachers' retirement system", 418(d)(6)(A) contemplates a system that "covers positions of employees of the State and positions of employees of one or more political subdivisions of the State", and POMS SL 30001.334 F.1 describes MERS as "a statewide system covering all municipal employees". Benefits from service for another entity count only as (d)(4)(ii) (a re-hired annuitant of the same system) and (e)(2)(v) allow. The April 1, 1998 edition, before either later amendment, states (c)(2) and its examples in the same words.
